$comment: NEW-1 (plan 3.7): the EXACT issue lifecycle a session drives, ONE rule ×4 (TS reference packages/domain-contract/src/issue-lifecycle.ts; the server applies it in lib/sessions/issue-lifecycle.ts; the natives move no status and only mirror the table when they render it, NEW-7). issueLifecycleTarget(event, state) = the ANCHOR status the issue moves to, or null = nothing moves. Events: `taken` = a WORKER session takes the issue: a session_issues row lands on a session that has a repository (`worker`: its branch comes at claim) through a link, issueIds on a start, a forward, a continuation, or a PERSON's message into such a session that holds it (bus rows never count); `pr_opened` = a PR links it; `pr_merged` = that PR landed in the default branch; `unlinked` = a worker dropped it; `filed` = a session CREATED the issue (EXP-1377: only when the create names it, sessionId or link: true = the caller's own; a create without either files an UNLINKED issue, never the caller's session by default): the row lands on the filer so the PR's share and the thread strip carry it, but filing is not working on it: nothing moves, in every state (the N-10 rule: an issue goes to In progress only when a session really takes it up). A later start, forward, link or a person's message into the filer takes it like any other row. State: `status` = the issue's anchor status (contract issueStatus), `openPr` = a live (open or draft) PR links it, `workers` = how many live sessions with a repository still hold it AFTER the event. Nothing else moves status: no settle-back when work stops, no move for a row on a session without a repository, no move on a message from a session. done, cancelled and duplicate never move here (people own them; a merge is the only automation into done). The team's PR automation (prOpened/prMerged targets, 'do nothing') maps the pr_* targets onto its rows as before; taken/unlinked always target the builtins.
